text: Let us dogfood the pilot on one real topic this week: my health insurance claim.
[fixture] Good choice. Decision: dogfood the pilot on the insurance claim. It has deadlines, documents and a few decisions.
Decision: the claim stays on local models only. I do not want the invoices in the cloud.
[fixture] Understood. The extract role runs on morrow, so the text stays on your network.
2 decisions so far. Add a reasoning map?
map: yes, pane added
dec-1 confirmed: dogfood the pilot on the insurance claim
dec-2 confirmed: the claim stays on local models only
What does the insurer need from me first?
[fixture] Usually the itemised invoice, the referral and the claim form. Task: scan the hospital invoice.
The invoice is here, I will scan it tonight.
[fixture] Fine. Their checklist is at https://example.org/claims/guide if you want to tick things off.
Should we write the letter with a paid cloud model? It writes better German.
[fixture] That would break your local-only decision. Decision: use a paid cloud model for the letter. Only if you change your mind.
dec-3 rejected: use a paid cloud model for the letter
No, keep it local. The letter can be plain.
[fixture] Then morrow drafts it and you polish it.
12 messages. Scrolling back gets slow. Add an index pane?
index: no, will ask again when the count has doubled
When is the deadline exactly?
[fixture] The letter says 30 days from the invoice date, so 2026-11-06.
Good. That is enough for today.
[fixture] Summary: two decisions, one task, the deadline is 2026-11-06.
task-1 confirmed: scan the hospital invoice
Back on the claim. I scanned the invoice yesterday.
[fixture] Good. Next is the call. Task: call the insurer about the deadline.
I called. They want the referral letter as well.
[fixture] Then the referral goes with the claim. Decision: send the referral together with the claim.
Can you remind me what we decided about the models?
[fixture] dec-2: the claim stays on local models only.
Right. Let us draft the letter now.
[fixture] A first outline: greeting, claim number, the three documents, one sentence on the deadline. Task: draft the claim letter.
24 messages. Scrolling back gets slow. Add an index pane?
index: yes, pane added
Decision: send it by registered mail, not the portal.
[fixture] Registered mail gives you a receipt with a date on it.
3 tasks have come up. Track them on a board?
kanban: no, will ask again when the count has doubled
task-2 confirmed: call the insurer about the deadline
dec-4 confirmed: send the referral together with the claim
dec-5 confirmed: send it by registered mail
task-3 confirmed: draft the claim letter
Should I also ask the hospital for an itemised bill?
[fixture] Only if the insurer asks for it. Decision: ask the hospital for an itemised bill. I would wait.
dec-6 rejected: ask the hospital for an itemised bill
Agreed, we wait. Enough for today.
[fixture] Summary: invoice scanned, insurer called, letter outlined, registered mail.
Letter day. Task: print the claim form.
[fixture] Noted. Task: sign the claim form after printing.
The referral is a photocopy, is that fine?
[fixture] Most insurers accept a copy. Task: ask the insurer whether a copy of the referral is enough.
6 tasks have come up. Track them on a board?
kanban: always, pane added; will not ask again
Decision: keep a copy of everything in one folder.
[fixture] One folder makes the receipt easy to find later.
Should the letter mention the 30-day deadline?
[fixture] Yes, in one sentence. Decision: mention the deadline in the first paragraph.
Decision: write the letter in English.
[fixture] Your insurer writes in German; I would answer in German.
dec-9 rejected: write the letter in English
Fine, German. Let me look back at the outline.
[fixture] The outline is in yesterday's reply about drafting the letter.
Done for today, thanks.
[fixture] Tomorrow: print, sign, send.
task-4 confirmed: print the claim form
task-5 confirmed: sign the claim form after printing
task-6 rejected: ask whether a copy of the referral is enough
Morning. Where did we leave the claim yesterday?
[fixture] You signed off with: print, sign, send. The letter draft is ready.
Show me the first line of the letter again.
[fixture] It opens with your policy number and the date of the hospital stay.
OK, the open proposals on the map, let me look at them.
[fixture] They are the registered-mail decision and the insurer form link.
dec-7 confirmed: keep a copy of everything in one folder
src-1 confirmed: insurer claim checklist
Is the policy number format right, with the dashes?
[fixture] Yes, the insurer writes it with dashes on its own forms.
The deadline was the end of the month, right?
[fixture] Yes, the insurer said the claim must arrive by the 31st.
How long does registered mail take here?
[fixture] Usually one to two working days inside the country.
Then sending on Monday is early enough.
[fixture] Yes, with a comfortable margin before the 31st.
What goes into the envelope, once more?
[fixture] The signed letter, the invoice copy, the referral and the claim form.
kanban pane faded to a tab: untouched for 8 turns (fadeAfterTurns 8). Click the tab to bring it back.
Let me scroll the index back to Tuesday.
[fixture] Tuesday has the first decisions and the scanned invoice.
Do I keep copies of everything?
[fixture] Yes, keep one copy of each page and the registered-mail receipt.
Where is the receipt usually kept?
[fixture] Many people staple it to their copy of the letter.
Remind me what the insurer said on the phone.
[fixture] They confirmed the referral must be attached, nothing else was missing.
Good. Anything about reimbursement time?
[fixture] They mentioned about four weeks after the claim arrives.
Let me check the index for the phone call.
[fixture] The call notes are in the session from the 15th.
Fine. I will print everything this evening.
[fixture] Sounds good. The letter is ready to print as it is.
